title: Magnetic Force Between Two Balls
prompt: In the universe Earth C-137, Rick has discovered a special form of magnetic force between two balls if they are put in his new invented basket. Rick has `n` empty baskets, the `i`-th basket is at `position[i]`, and he has `m` balls to distribute. He wants to distribute the balls into the baskets to maximize the minimum magnetic force between any two balls. The magnetic force between two balls at positions `x` and `y` is `abs(x - y)`. Given the integer array `position` and the integer `m`, return the required force.

examples.explanation: Placing the 3 balls at positions 1, 4, and 7 gives a minimum pairwise distance of 3, which is the maximum possible.

constraints: all integers in position are distinct
hints: Trying every possible minimum distance from 1 upward and checking whether it's achievable works, but the distance can be as large as 10^9, so a linear scan of distances is too slow.

Sort the positions first. For a fixed candidate minimum distance d, you can greedily place balls left to right, only placing a new ball when it's at least d away from the last placed one, and count how many balls fit.
The number of balls that fit is monotonically non-increasing as d grows, so binary search on d itself for the largest value where at least m balls fit.

solution.approach: Sort the positions, then binary search on the candidate minimum force d, ranging from 1 to the full span of positions. For a given d, greedily place the first ball at the first position and then scan left to right, placing the next ball only once the current position is at least d away from the last placed ball; count how many balls this greedy placement fits. This count is monotonically non-increasing as d increases, so binary search for the largest d for which at least m balls still fit, giving an O(n log(max position)) solution.
